Data:Slnev.visiting.timothy.morgen.json.startdescription: Reverend Timothy sits next to Morgen and, initially, clearly finds her quite charming. He chatters happily away about his time in Brancrug and at theological college and eventually asks her about her background. He grows increasingly puzzled and when she mentions her 'un-sisters' the penny clearly drops. He moves his chair as far away from her as is politely possible and avoids conversation for the rest of the meal. She smiles and offers to cut up his food for him. [Lesson: Wolf Stories]

Data:Slnev.visiting.timothy.olympe.json.startdescription: Reverend Timothy learns that Olympe is (at least sometimes) editor of the Kerisham Review. He is eager to offer her work he's written on the films of Ilse Bischoff. She puts him off with practised smoothness but his endless enthusiasm for Bischovian detail wears her down, then seems to win her over, and by the end of the meal she has given him her card. [Lesson: Disciplines of the Scar]

Data:Slnev.visiting.timothy.serena.json.startdescription: Timothy has questions for Serena about the Church in Alexandria, the cult of St Lucia, and various instances of syncretism with pre-Solar beliefs. She does her best to answer him. [Lesson: Sacra Solis Invicti]

Data:Slnev.visiting.timothy.stanislav.js.startdescription: Timothy is a doctor of theology: a qualification which has apparently been a source of confusion in Brancrug, where a number of villagers have taken 'doctor' to mean they should ask him for help with their aches and sprains. He dislikes turning them away, and prevails on Stanislav for some practical advice. [Lesson: Herbs & Infusions]

Data:Slnev.visiting.timothy.yvette.json.startdescription: Reverend Timothy is discussing historical heresies and heterodoxies with Yvette. She seems moderately engaged by the conversation, but Reverend Tim is fairly boiling with excitement. [Lesson: Watchman's Paradoxes]

Data:Slnev.visiting.timothy.zachary.json.startdescription: Reverend Timothy talks excitedly to Zachary about eggs, clocks, the local badger population and his housekeeper's black pudding. Eventually he notices that Zachary isn't really paying attention, and that Zachary's expression is not cheerful. In a softer tone, he begins to explicate St Lewen's discourses on endings and beginnings. [Lesson: Auroral Contemplations]

Data:Slnev.yvette.agdistis.json.startdescription: Yvette listens as Agdistis grapples with his dislike of Solomon Husher's work: he cannot, will not, accept that everything must end - he is unwilling even to accept that anything must end. [Lesson: Sights & Sensations]

Data:Slnev.yvette.aladim.json.startdescription: Yvette asks al-Adim what he remembers of his parents. He replies that he recalls only their deaths. He speaks of those deaths with a dispassion that seems to surprise him more than it does her. [Lesson: Wolf Stories]

Data:Slnev.yvette.arthur.json.startdescription: Yvette raises the subject of Sabazine again with Athur. She has been reading of the god Sabazos, who brings madness by deploying the weapons of speech-in-silence. Arthur has heard of these techniques, and very cautiously shares a very little… [Lesson: Sharps]

Data:Slnev.yvette.arun.json.startdescription: Arun and Yvette began with a serious philological discussion - the similarities between Henavek and Vak - but the conversation has devolved into something more like gossip, comparing the virtues and charms of Vak and Henavek as if they were individuals. Arun mentions the tradition that the two languages are brother and sister. 'It would be a shame, wouldn't it, if they were?' Yvette responds archly. 'If they were brother and sister, nothing unsuitable could occur between them, surely?' Arun's whole face creases in an unusually fervent smile. [Lesson: Henavek]

Data:Slnev.yvette.azita.json.startdescription: In one History, Alexander heard a secret from Darius that convinced him to abandon battle and return home, announcing, 'the Sun has his course, and so do I.' Yvette asks Azita what she knows about the secret, apparently under the impression that Azita and Alexander were contemporaries, which causes Azita some amusement ('I'm not even a thousand years old'). In any case the Azita is of the opinion that the secret is 'a Lionsmith nonsense' and Alexander was 'much overestimated.' [Lesson: Sickle & Eclipse]

Data:Slnev.yvette.chaima.json.startdescription: Yvette questions Chaima about the motives and credibility of 'Little Sophia', the monster-hunting, and specifically Worm-hunting, author of 'Oblations in Iron'. Chaima is non-commital, but very clear that she herself tries not to hunt Worms. [Lesson: Inks of Containment]

Data:Slnev.yvette.connie.json.startdescription: Connie and Yvette are discussing a patient of Yvette's who, it now appears, may have died before attending his first session. ('I had wondered,' Yvette says slowly, 'why my rooms were always so cold afterwards.') Connie is of the opinion that since the man is dead, no ethical considerations about confidentiality need apply. Yvette is not convinced. [Lesson: Rhyme & Remembrance]

Data:Slnev.yvette.coquille.json.startdescription: Coquille presses Yvette on her resemblance to Rowena Hengerst; she asks whether they have ever met. 'No,' says Yvette; 'she will never agree to an interview with me.' Coquille theorises eagerly about why; Yvette nods and smiles. [Lesson: Sea Stories]

Data:Slnev.yvette.corso.json.startdescription: Yvette presses Corso on the origins of the 'Codex Acephali'. He answers her as best he can, but then changes the subject: 'I don't want to talk about that book when I'm eating.' [Lesson: Snow Stories]

Data:Slnev.yvette.dagmar.json.startdescription: Dagmar talks to Yvette of her dreams of the Painted River. 'Hard to tell if it's a dream of the River, or in the River. River's behind the Stag Door. Never passed the Stag Door; well, not formally speaking; well, let's not talk about that, eh? But anyway the Vagabond painted the River, and her whole thing, y'see, is she gets in where she's not meant to. Actually shall we talk about something else?' [Lesson: Pearl & Tide]

Data:Slnev.yvette.douglas.json.startdescription: Yvette and Douglas discuss stymphlings, which Douglas calls 'the Dove-Hour's mistake', and Yvette prefers to think of as a blessed memory of a redder-sun age… [Lesson: Rhyme & Remembrance]

Data:Slnev.yvette.ehsan.json.startdescription: Yvette and Ehsan speak wistfully of what they have read of the lost Hour called Tide. Yvette recalls that when the Sister withdraws, other Hours sometimes fill the space left by her withdrawal, and wonders whether the Tide is gentle enough to remain afterwards... but Ehsan politely insists that the gods-who-were-stone are never gentle. [Lesson: Pearl & Tide]

Data:Slnev.yvette.fraser.json.startdescription: Yvette and Fraser discuss his further 'dreams of eyes', and his theories about the entry of the Scīmafectra-kind and the Thritige-kind to human flesh. Yvette wonders aloud whether he has ever considered that most - perhaps all - of the dreams arise from his own frustrated desire for fatherhood. In a fit of temper, he snatches off the glove on his changed hand, and displays its glossy, altered angles to her. For a moment there is silence at the table. [Lesson: Pentiments & Precursors]

Data:Slnev.yvette.hokobald.json.startdescription: Yvette asks Hokobald whether there are ways to determine who might be a child of two Long. He insists with apparent pride that it is very rare for the children of Long to survive - that one of their parents almost always devours them and 'ascends' to alukite status - but acknowledges that it has been known, under rare circumstances, and shares some of the signs... [Lesson: Resurgences & Emergences]

Data:Slnev.yvette.morgen.json.startdescription: Emboldened by their last conversation, Yvette asks pointed questions about how Morgen came to be what she is. Morgen won't talk about how she went alukite, but she does talk about growing Long - her tutoring in the Old Form by Sulochana, her fascination with the Thunderskin's New Form, and the last dances which took her to the House of the Moon. [Lesson: Tridesma Hiera]

Data:Slnev.yvette.olympe.json.startdescription: Yvette and Olympe continue their theorising about the fundamentally fabulous or metaphorical nature of the gods-who-were-stone. Perhaps the Flint is only a cooling shard of the Forge's impulses - perhaps the Tide represents the Grail's unconscious desire for peace.... Olympe proposes to commission Yvette to write a series of articles for the Kerisham Review. [Lesson: Putrefactions & Calcinations]

Data:Slnev.yvette.serena.json.startdescription: Serena and Yvette discuss the death of the Marcher Lord Gwilym Ddu, 'Black William', in which the nuns of St Brandan's might - might - have been implicated through their dealings with the old powers of the hills… Yvette brightly suggests there might have been some linguistic confusion between 'Gwilym Ddu' and 'Kelemdu', the Black Dove... but Serena puts her finger to her lips. [Lesson: Rhyme & Remembrance]

Data:Slnev.yvette.stanislav.json.startdescription: Yvette and Stanislav chat about the notorious erotic-occult novel, 'Ettery After', which Yvette considers 'flimsy' and Stanislav considers 'saucy'. [Lesson: Inks of Containment]

Data:Slnev.yvette.visiting.denzil.json.startdescription: Yvette does her best to put Denzil at his ease: he is plainly very wary of her. He remains polite, but taciturn even by his own taciturn standards. He does eventually admit that in Brancrug, there is a traidition that it is bad luck to insult, or to buy from, or to drink with a pale-haired woman... [Lesson: Sea Stories]

Data:Slnev.yvette.visiting.killes.json.startdescription: Yvette, unexpectedly, asks if she can paint Mrs Kille. Mrs Kille, no less surprisingly, agrees - 'been a while' - but asks Yvette detailed questions about her technique. Mr Kille pays close, albeit unobtrusive, attention. [Lesson: Sights & Sensations]

Data:Slnev.yvette.visiting.timothy.json.startdescription: Yvette and Reverend Timothy are discussing differences between the Received and Sanctioned versions of the Book of Suns. Yvette, whose formal theological education ended with Sunday school, is clearly confused by the details, but this only makes Reverend Tim more eager to correct her, and his innocent enthusiasm is making her smile. [Lesson: Sacra Solis Invicti]

Data:Slnev.yvette.zachary.json.startdescription: Yvette is speaking soothingly to Zachary of snow, silence, and the full moon… [Lesson: Snow Stories]

Data:Slnev.zachary.agdistis.json.startdescription: Zachary describes his understanding of the 'Angel of Storms', the beauty of her underclouds, the accesses of her lightning, how he yearns to cage her in glass. Agdistis listens patiently; now and then his eyes flicker as if he understands. [Lesson: Quenchings & Quellings]

Data:Slnev.zachary.aladim.json.startdescription: Zachary, unselfconsciously, recites a poem-in-progress to al-Adim: a clashing fortress of a piece. He beats out the rhythm on the tabletop. Al-Adim tentatively suggests a refinement, which Zachary, judiciously, accepts. [Lesson: Preliminal Meter]

Data:Slnev.zachary.arthur.json.startdescription: Zachary and Arthur discuss a prophecy of the War of the Roads, in which the Imperishable Legions war with the Leashed Flame, to apocalyptic effect. Arthur fears that the prophecy is not yet complete - that it refers to a coming war in Europe. Zachary agrees, but finds it difficult to articulate his reasons - he says that the Imperishable Legions are not the Légion du Seuil, but (gesturing, ever gesturing) that they are 'yoked at the Heart.' [Lesson: Ragged Crossroads]

Data:Slnev.zachary.arun.json.startdescription: 'Remember,' Arun tells Zachary, 'that it's always too late, eventually; but it never is until then.' Zachary lets out a long sigh. 'You always say that. It's less helpful than you think it is.' [Lesson: Putrefactions & Calcinations]

Data:Slnev.zachary.azita.json.startdescription: Zachary and Azita compare exorcism techniques. She asks jokingly what techniques might be used to exorcise him, and immediately regrets it when he doesn't realise she's joking and answers as seriously as he can. [Lesson: Sickle & Eclipse]

Data:Slnev.zachary.chaima.json.startdescription: Zachary and Chaima talk about how it is when the hunt ends - the uneasy space before the next begins. [Lesson: Ragged Crossroads]

Data:Slnev.zachary.chaima.seventhvoice.j.startdescription: Zachary recites some of the passages from Savage's 'A Seventh Voice' that Dagmar chortlingly shared with him. His clear, chilly, precise diction has an unexpected effect: the risqué elements seem poignant, the poignant elements shimmer with light. Chaima takes his hand as she listens, and the restless movement of his fingers briefly stills. [Lesson: Preliminal Meter]

Data:Slnev.zachary.connie.json.startdescription: Connie and Zachary are discussing the effects of his tattoos-of-containment plan to help with his condition. It's not promising. He shows Connie his forearm, on which the tattoos are already fading like flower-colours under frost. 'You must come in,' she tells him. 'To the Bureau. Before it's too late. It's getting hard to explain why I haven't brought you in already...' [Lesson: Inks of Containment]

Data:Slnev.zachary.coquille.json.startdescription: Zachary and Coquille swap parables of the 'Great Scar' - the goddess-language Vak, who is the Peacock Door - and of how she might be healed. Coquille points out that would be the end of Vak. 'Yes,' Zachary agrees, 'the end of her pain.' [Lesson: The Great Signs and the Great Scars]

Data:Slnev.zachary.corso.json.startdescription: Zachary wants more help from Corso with his Hyksos studies. He's heard that the ceremonies of the Légion du Seuil sometimes employ that language. He's considering joining the Légion, but he wants to understand it better first. [Lesson: Hyksos]

Data:Slnev.zachary.dagmar.json.startdescription: Zachary shows Dagmar a Tanglebrag he's made. He tries to explain how it 'portrays and betrays' the paths of his future. She tries to understand. [Lesson: Edicts Liminal]

Data:Slnev.zachary.douglas.json.startdescription: Zachary and Douglas reminisce about a case they both worked on, years ago, when they had to find a way to bind a thriceros which had somehow found its way into the Thames. Douglas recalls how the binding-process first awakened his enthusiasm for knitting, and Zachary makes the necessary effort to fold his face into a smile. [Lesson: Quenchings & Quellings]
